qwen3.8-27b-aq3.display_name: AryaInfer Qwen3.8 27B GSQ3 AQ3 - 128K vision (Arya engine, faster writing)
qwen3.8-27b-aq3.notes: ISTA-DASLab's 3-bit GSQ checkpoint repacked as AQ3 (tools/aryainfer_gsq3_convert.py), uniform 3-bit with a scale per 128, read only by aryainfer.exe. Measured on this host 2026-11-03, final build: reading 1,444-1,633 tok/s at 8K (batch 2,048; 1,266 at batch 512, 711 before the Q8_0 expansion was made coalesced) and 1,153.9-1,175.0 on a 62K prompt (batch 2,048, 64K context; 990 before the attention work); 968.7 on a 61,787-token prompt through the server at 131K context (15.2 GiB, before that work); writing 88-104 tok/s at 8K. The prompt attention keeps its scores as halves and uses bigger key blocks, taking its share of 62K prefill from 39% (24.4 s) to 35% (18.8 s). Entry paths repaired 2026-11-03 (they held UNC paths that do not resolve) and the vision encoder points at the AQ3 file; an image turn was checked. Batch 1024 is its setting: 2048 at 131K would add ~1.4 GiB on a card that measured 15.2 GiB. PLC/HMI calibration 2026-11-05 (docs/PLC_SAMPLING.md): the eight-fixture industrial suite scored the low-temperature set best (0.3 / 0.9 / 20 / 0.0), which it now ships, and the four thinking levels each rendered their own request (off silent, low/medium/high 1,432-1,650 reasoning chars). Every reasoning budget is 20% higher: low 4,800, medium 9,600, high 12,000.

qwen3.8-27b-turbo-iq3xxs.display_name: AryaInfer Qwen3.8 27B Turbo Brilliance IQ3_XXS (MTP) - 128K vision
qwen3.8-27b-turbo-iq3xxs.notes: DavidAU's Qwen3.8 27B Turbo Brilliance 50X Reasoning-Instruct (GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, MTP) on the Arya engine (aryainfer.exe): a 27B dense fine-tune of Qwen3.8-27B with 27 reasoning + 27 instruct + 9 xhigh modes driven by {REASON:...} tags, 3.05 bpw mixed GSQ-RCO quants, 10.4 GB. The context was raised from 102,400 to 131,072 after the runs below were taken, so the 805.4 figure was measured at 100K. Measured on this host 2026-11-03: reading 1,241.9 tok/s at 8K prompt/32K context and 805.4 on a 99K prompt at 100K context (batch 1,024); writing 57.3 and 52.5 tok/s with the MTP draft (20/28 and 8/11 accepted). Thinking modes: off 4/6 probes, low/medium/high 6/6 each; sampling calibration (0.6/0.95/20): 10 requests, no loops, 6/7 code probes (one hit the 300-token cap), 3/3 adherence, mean 4-gram diversity 0.89. Kept as the daily driver after a first-try animated-HTML task. PLC/HMI calibration 2026-11-05 (docs/PLC_SAMPLING.md): 0.3 / 0.9 / 20 / 0.0 scored highest of four sets, replacing 0.7 / 0.95 / 64, and the display name now says 128K because the context has been 131,072 since it was raised. All four thinking levels reach the model. Budgets are 20% higher (high 14,400).

qwen3.6-35b-a3b-abliterated.notes: wangzhang's Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-abliterated Q4_K_M (19.7 GiB), text only, on the Poly engine (strata-poly.exe). Measured on this host 2026-11-03, warm: reading 2,006.2 tok/s on an 8K prompt at 32K context and 1,770.0 on a 128K prompt at 131K context (prompt batch 512, Q8_0 KV); writing 83.1 and 41.8 tok/s, the quickest of the four Qwen3.6 files here at both lengths even without an MTP draft block. Sampling calibration (0.6/0.95/20) on 10 coding requests: 7/7 Python/C#/SQL fixtures, 3/3 adherence, mean 4-gram diversity 0.99, no loops. Thinking modes: off 5/6 probes but low, medium and high 4/6 each, so this one is best run with thinking off; it also writes much longer answers than the APEX profile. Shipped tuned to the measured settings: default reasoning effort off (thinking scored 4/6 against 5/6 with it off), and temperature 0.6 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 20 / presence 0.0, which is what the coding suite above ran. It reads images with the base Qwen3.6-35B-A3B vision encoder (mmproj-F16 from UD-Q4_K_XL): wangzhang's repo ships weights only, but abliteration edits text-layer weights, so the tower and projector are unchanged. Verified on this host 2026-11-03 by reading a synthetic card as ARYA-5907 exactly, at 1,086 prompt tokens with the 1,024-token image floor. Re-tuned 2026-11-05 (docs/PLC_SAMPLING.md): 0.3 / 0.9 / 20 / 0.0 scored highest, and the default effort is off again (the config says "none"), which the thinking probes support. The runtime config also regained the vision block the other 35B entries already had, so the app lists it as multimodal again. Budgets are 20% higher (high 12,000).

qwen3.5-4b.display_name: AryaStrata Qwen3.5 4B Q4_K_M - 64K vision (pairs with ComfyUI)
qwen3.5-4b.notes: Unsloth Qwen3.5-4B Q4_K_M (2,740,937,888 B) with mmproj-F16 (672,423,616 B) on the dense qwen35 path of strata-poly (aryainfer.exe), --kv q4_0, 64K context. Added 2026-11-06 to run beside ComfyUI: resident it holds about 4.5 GiB of the 16 GB card, and on 2026-11-06 it ran in the same second as ComfyUI's qwen_image_2.1 unet, VAE and GPU text encoder (peak 13.85 GiB of 16.38 GiB used). Measured with ComfyUI idle and the engine resident: 20-67 token prompts decoded at 141-163 tok/s with 0.07-0.30 s to the first token; a 1,063-token image turn decoded at 140-157 tok/s (first picture 7.77 s because the CPU image encoder runs then, later turns reuse the embedding). A 1024 cutout through ComfyUI took 28.1 s with the engine resident, 8.1 s with it unloaded, and 100.2 s when ComfyUI's text encoder was forced onto the CPU - so the encoder stays on the GPU and ComfyUI pages its unet instead. Vision: strata-vision.exe on the CPU (gpu:false) encodes on first sight only; 1,036 image tokens from a 640x480 PNG in 7.4 s, 1.05 GiB peak RAM. Every tensor name and shape the dense qwen35 loader reads is present (426 tensors, 24 GDN + 8 attention layers, no mismatches) and every geometry check in qwen35.cpp passes; the GGUF has no MTP block, so --no-draft is not needed. Tokenizer pack C:\AI\Strata-data\packs\qwen35-4b\tokenizer built with tools/strata_tokenizer.py (248,320 vocab, 247,587 merges, 16/16 round trips); its chat template is the official Qwen3.5 template with two edits: tool arguments that arrive as a JSON string are parsed with from_json instead of raising (DSH sends tool_calls that way), and thinking stays off unless enable_thinking is true. Sampling 0.7 / 0.8 / 20 / presence 1.5, thinking off by default with budgets low 2,048 / medium 4,096 / high 8,192.
